title: The Rutgers visit and hearing 'Stop, You're Breaking My Heart' again
summary: Maxine's mini-tour at Rutgers on 17 July and her reaction when her son played the old record.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: Bernice Reape has left us now. And for the next few minutes, we're just going to go over some bits and pieces left over from the last interview session that we did.

S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC.

I'm just trying to recover from my visit and my mini-tour at Rutgers Institute of Jazz Studies we made last week.
Oh yes. That was on the 17th of July.

Yes, the 17th of July. Strangely enough, I had attended Rutgers University in 1960 which is twenty years ago in a crash course in community leadership for the community. This is doing the time that I was in retirement. And I had no idea that I'd be getting back to Rutgers to visit the Jazz Institute, because as I said before, I had considered myself pretty much out of it in 1960. But I really enjoyed the tour, and I had a chance to bring myself up to date on a lot of the things that I had been doing in the past. Some of the things that I had forgotten and some dates which I wasn't too sure about myself.

to handle -- that's Vocalion 3616, of 'Stop, You're Breaking My Heart.'

Yeah, that was really something.

The funny thing about that, I had forgotten all about 'Stop, You're Breaking My Heart' completely.

It was one of the selections we did on that first record date that I made when I first came to New York.

And when my son played it for me a couple of months ago, I listened to the arrangement and it sounded familiar. And I couldn't figure it out quite completely.

And then, when the vocal started, I feel like Bernice did just a while ago, 'That's me!'
Yeah. You were telling us about that (inaudible).
